title: Tesla to report earnings after Elon Musk floats SpaceX merger plan
detail:
Tesla to report earnings after Elon Musk floats SpaceX merger plan
Dara Kerr
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 12:41 PM MST 3 min read

A Tesla dealership in Santa Clarita, California. Wall Street has projected Tesla to report $27.9bn in revenues.Photograph: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Investors will be paying close attention to Tesla's third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, after chief executive Elon Musk floated the idea of merging the car company with his rocket and AI company, SpaceX. On a call with SpaceX investors on Tuesday, Musk said: "There's a lot of merit to combining the companies."

Musk said that the board of directors for both of his businesses had put together special committees to explore the potential merger, but had not yet reached an agreement on the terms of the transaction. The move would require the approval of 50% of all Tesla shareholders.

Related: Tesla and SpaceX explore merger as Elon Musk gives backing

For Tesla's earnings on Wednesday, Wall Street is projecting the electric vehicle company to report a revenue of $27.9bn, with 43 cents on earnings per share. That would put the company at a slightly lower revenue than last quarter, which came in with $28.23bn in revenue.

Tesla has experienced a rough year with falling stock and increased competition from cheaper Chinese automakers. The company's share price has fallen by more than 11% this year, although it appears to have rebounded some since last week with the news of the possible SpaceX merger.

Last week, Musk unveiled the company's electric sports car, the Roadster 2, which he said uses technology from SpaceX to "basically fly like a rocket". At a demonstration at a SpaceX facility in Texas, a remote-controlled version of the car drove up a steeply curved ramp and then used jet-like thrusters to flip over, hover and land. The vehicle is priced at upwards of $200,000.

"Flying cars are real … it can basically fly like a rocket, it can do rolls, crazy gymnastics," Musk said at the event, adding that "I'm not sure it's necessarily legal in all jurisdictions."

Tesla's vehicle sales are not as crucial to its market performance as they once were, as the company has pivoted towards robotics, autonomous driving and AI. Tesla's Optimus robot has faced production hurdles, however; and its driverless taxi service, Robotaxi, has hit road blocks in scaling its fleet and expanding to new cities.

Musk has long declared the Robotaxi will have near-infinite demand and that "probably half the population of the US" would be using the autonomous ride-hailing service by the end of 2025. Similarly, the CEO has forecast the manufacture of as many as 1m Optimus robots each year. As is frequently the case with Musk's promises, he has failed to reach those lofty targets and rollout has been slow.

Tech stocks were higher late Wednesday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 1.6% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) adding 1.9%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index climbed 1.9%.

In corporate news, Meta Platforms (META) was ordered to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury determined the tech giant was liable for deceiving Facebook users about privacy policies, according to media reports. Meta shares were up 1.3%.

SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) have formed special committees to evaluate a potential merger, Elon Musk, who heads both companies, said late Tuesday. SpaceX shares jumped 7%, and Tesla rose 3.4%.

Super Micro Computer's (SMCI) shares surged nearly 10% after it reported preliminary fiscal Q1 revenue and margin results above expectations late Tuesday.

Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google CEO Sundar Pichai received a letter Wednesday from Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) asking for information on the impact the company's AI products have had on the mental health and educational development of children, The Wall Street Journal reported. Alphabet shares were down 1.7%.
